summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with low-grade fever, malaise, and increased abdominal distension. He had recently been exposed to a family member with cold symptoms. Workup included negative blood, urine, and ascites cultures, ruling out bacteremia and spontaneous bacterial peritonitis. Imaging showed stable cirrhosis and new but non-urgent findings in the liver and lung. His symptoms were attributed to a viral upper respiratory infection, which improved with supportive care including fluticasone. A therapeutic paracentesis removed 2 liters of fluid. Nutrition recommended reducing tube feeding duration from 18 to 16 hours daily due to suspected caloric excess. He remained stable on his transplant regimen, including Remodulin for portopulmonary hypertension. He was discharged home with improved symptoms and follow-up planned with his liver team.
problems: Acute upper respiratory infections of unspecified site
Esophageal varices in diseases classified elsewhere, without mention of bleeding
Cirrhosis of liver without mention of alcohol
Chronic hepatitis C without mention of hepatic coma
